title: Are We Recovering Mechanisms? Objective-Level Recovery Gaps in Mechanistic Interpretability
abstract: arXiv:2610.02098v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Mechanistic interpretability aims to recover the internal computations responsible for model behavior. Progress in automated circuit discovery is often framed as a search problem: better attribution or optimization should identify better mechanisms. This assumes that the evaluation objective can recognize a better circuit once it is found. We show that intervention-defined faithfulness can instead prefer an equally sized circuit that reproduces the model's behavior less well, creating an objective-level recovery gap. Across four human-reference tasks and InterpBench, we compare validation faithfulness with behavior on held-out prompts under fixed ordinary resampling. The behavioral criterion is agreement with the intact model, including its mistakes, except on Greater-Than, where we use semantic accuracy. translated_title: 我们真的在恢复机制吗？机制可解释性中的目标层面恢复差距
translated_abstract: 机制可解释性旨在恢复模型行为背后的内部计算。自动化电路发现的进展通常被构建为一个搜索问题：更好的归因或优化方法应该能够识别出更好的机制。这隐含地假设了评估目标能够在找到更好的电路后识别出它。我们证明，由干预定义的忠实度反而可能更偏好一个同样大小但复制模型行为能力较差的电路，从而产生了目标层面的恢复差距。在四个人类参考任务和InterpBench上，我们在固定的普通重采样条件下，比较了验证忠实度与模型在保留提示上的行为表现。行为准则是与完整模型的一致性（包括其错误），但在Greater-Than任务上我们使用语义准确性。受控的参考编辑实验揭示了无需任何发现算法即可出现的排名错误，而EAP、EAP-IG、ACDC和Edge-SP的输出表现出……
tldr: 该研究揭示了机制可解释性中的目标层面恢复差距：干预定义的忠实度评估指标可能偏好同样大小但行为复制较差的电路，导致评估目标无法识别真正更好的机制。
en_tdlr: The study reveals an objective-level recovery gap in mechanistic interpretability: intervention-defined faithfulness can prefer equally sized circuits that reproduce model behavior less well, causing the evaluation objective to fail at recognizing truly better mechanisms.
